plan_or_price_mentions: Use our models with pay-as-you-go billing on Meta Model API and in Muse Code , or in Muse Code with a monthly subscription . This page covers pay-as-you-go: Model API bills the reasoning models (Muse Wonder, Muse Spark, and Muse Ember) per token, image generation per image, Muse Voice Transcribe by the hour of audio processed, and Segment Anything Model (SAM) per image or video frame segmented, with no minimums or upfront commitment.

Web search grounding : $2.50 per 1,000 search queries , in addition to the request's token cost. This applies to the web_search tool on the reasoning models, Muse Wonder , Muse Spark , and Muse Ember .
capability_mentions: Use our models with pay-as-you-go billing on Meta Model API and in Muse Code , or in Muse Code with a monthly subscription . This page covers pay-as-you-go: Model API bills the reasoning models (Muse Wonder, Muse Spark, and Muse Ember) per token, image generation per image, Muse Voice Transcribe by the hour of audio processed, and Segment Anything Model (SAM) per image or video frame segmented, with no minimums or upfront commitment.
These apply to the reasoning models above.

Web search grounding : $2.50 per 1,000 search queries , in addition to the request's token cost. This applies to the web_search tool on the reasoning models, Muse Wonder , Muse Spark , and Muse Ember .
Muse Image 's built-in web and image search is part of its per-image price and isn't charged separately. See Muse Image pricing .

Muse Image is billed at a flat rate per generated image. The price is the same regardless of prompt length, reasoning_strength , or the tools the model uses during generation, including its built-in web and image search, which isn't charged separately. A request that returns n images is billed for n images. You're billed only for images the model successfully generates and returns: images that fail to generate, or that are removed by safety filtering before they're returned, aren't counted. Imag
Muse Voice Transcribe is billed by audio processed, metered in whole seconds.

Streaming and non-streaming transcription are priced the same. Zero data retention (ZDR) is priced at parity with Standard mode. Contributor mode isn't available for Muse Voice Transcribe. Audio time is billed as a separate line item from token usage, rounded down to whole seconds; other endpoints aren't billed for audio time.

SAM 3.1 segmentation is billed per image and per video frame, not per token. The same prices apply to streaming and non-streaming requests. Each video request is billed for at least 50 frames, so a clip or tracking range shorter than 50 frames is billed as 50. The response's usage.video_frames_processed reports the frames billed for that request.
muse-voice-transcribe-1.0 None None 256 concurrent streams; 16,000 streams per hour
SAM 3.1 is billed per image or frame and Muse Image is priced per image , so neither has a TPM limit.

Muse Voice Transcribe is billed by audio processed , so it's limited by streams rather than requests or tokens. Concurrent streams caps how many transcription sessions you hold open at once; streams per hour caps how many you start. Realtime and file transcription share the same budget.

A realtime stream rejected for exceeding a stream limit closes with 1013 . A rejected file-transcription request returns HTTP 429 Too Many Requests . Transcription responses don't include the x-ratelimit-* headers.

document_observations.title: Subscriptions - Meta Model API
plan_or_price_mentions: With a Muse Code subscription, you pay a flat monthly rate for usage of Muse Code , instead of paying per token. Subscription benefits and availability may vary by region. Available benefits will be shown to you during onboarding before you subscribe.

To sign up for a Muse Code subscription, you will need a Meta Account. Using your Meta Account, you can create an associated Meta Model API account and sign up for a subscription. The subscription applies to the Muse Code API key that is automatically connected in the Muse Code CLI onboarding process. This credential is for use with Muse Code only. Any additional API keys you create under your Meta Model API account will be billed through pay-as-you-go .

You must be 18 or the age of majority in your country to subscribe. Your subscription is subject to the Meta Subscription Terms of Service (opens in new tab) , and your use of Muse Code and the Meta Model API is governed by the Meta Model API Terms of Service and the Meta Model API Acceptable Use Policy .
There are 4 subscription plans available for Muse Code:
Everything from the Everyday Usage plan
5x more usage than the Everyday Usage plan
Everything from the High Usage plan
20x more usage than the Everyday Usage plan
Everything from the Power Usage plan
80x more usage than the Everyday Usage plan

Muse Code subscriptions default to Contributor mode. In Contributor mode, you get more usage from your plan in exchange for letting Meta use your content to train future Meta models. Contributor mode is a setting in Muse Code, and you can turn it off at any time, at which point your future content is not used to train Meta models (unless you turn it back on in your settings).
Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full are each available in either mode on the plans that include them. For the models each plan includes, see Muse Wonder availability .
The Contributor mode row appears only while you're signed in with an active Muse Code subscription. It doesn't appear if:
Subscription : a flat monthly rate (see the plans above). It works only through the Muse Code CLI while signed in with your Meta Model API account.

If you reach your plan's usage limit, you can upgrade to the next plan, or wait until your limit refreshes. If you are on the Maximum Usage plan, you must wait for your limit to refresh. Usage through any additional API keys you create is billed pay-as-you-go.
Select Muse Code , then choose a plan and complete checkout.
On success, you will see a confirmation screen with a link to your receipt and the option to Manage your subscription .
Manage your plan from Manage your subscription on the Subscriptions page in Accounts Center (opens in new tab) . From an interactive session, type /upgrade to open Accounts Center in your browser.
Upgrade : A plan upgrade takes effect immediately. You will be charged a prorated amount for the rest of the current billing cycle.
Downgrade : A plan downgrade takes effect at the start of your next billing cycle. You will keep your current plan's usage limit until the next billing cycle.

Cancel : From Accounts Center, go to Manage your subscription and select Cancel subscription . Your subscription stays active until the end of the current billing cycle, then you lose access to all benefits. Cancel at least 24 hours before your next billing date to avoid future charges.
What happens when your subscription ends
A subscription ends one of 2 ways: you can cancel it (see Change or cancel your plan ), or Meta can revoke it.

Revocation is different from cancellation. When your subscription is revoked, you lose access immediately instead of at the end of your billing cycle. Meta may revoke a subscription for various reasons, including:
Policy violation : your account violates the Model API terms , Meta's Community Standards (opens in new tab) or Meta Subscription Terms of Service (opens in new tab) .

Account deletion or deactivation : deleting your account cancels the subscription immediately. Deactivating your account keeps the subscription active for 30 days. If you don't reactivate within that window, Meta revokes it.

Your subscription renews automatically each month on the date you first subscribed. If that date doesn't exist in a given month (for example, the 31st in a 30-day month), you're charged on the last day of that month instead.
No refunds for canceled subscriptions : if you cancel your subscription, you won't receive a credit or refund unless required by law.

document_observations.title: API reference — Meta Model API - Meta Model API
api_mentions: Meta Model API is an HTTP API served at https://api.meta.ai/v1 and authenticated with a bearer token. This reference documents each resource's request and response schema. For a task-oriented introduction, start with the Quickstart ; to choose a request format, see Choosing an API .
Responses : POST /v1/responses and related endpoints — server-managed, agentic generation with reasoning replay. OpenAI-compatible.
Chat completions : POST /v1/chat/completions — the OpenAI-compatible messages-array endpoint.
Messages : POST /v1/messages — the Anthropic Messages-compatible endpoint.
Files : POST /v1/files (upload), GET /v1/files (list), GET / DELETE /v1/files/{file_id} (retrieve/delete a single file) — upload and manage files referenced in requests.
Models : GET /v1/models — list available models and retrieve model details.

tables.heading: Query parameters
rows: Correlation id used in server-side logs and echoed in the response. When omitted, the server generates one.

capability_mentions: Transcribe a recording - Meta Model API
Transcribe one complete audio recording in a single request.

Send multipart/form-data with two parts: request , the transcription settings as JSON, and audio , the clip. The Accept header selects between a buffered JSON body, a server-sent event stream, and plain text.

HTTP 200 — The transcript, in the shape selected by Accept . application/json , */* , or an absent header returns the buffered body. text/event-stream returns the realtime event stream, which ends after the last event and appends no summary. text/plain returns one turn per line in ENDPOINTING , or lines of the form A:Hello in DIARIZATION (a turn the model never attributed renders as unknown:<transcript> ).
HTTP 400 — The audio is not a supported WAV file, the audio exceeds 10 minutes, or the body is not multipart/form-data .

HTTP 500 — Transcription failed, or processing exceeded the server budget. Once an event stream has started there is no status left to set, so the failure arrives as a terminal error event on the open stream under HTTP 200 .
For audio conversion, modes, and worked examples, see the Speech to text feature page.

capability_mentions: Transcribe in realtime - Meta Model API
Stream audio over a WebSocket and receive transcripts, turn boundaries, and speaker labels as the audio arrives.

Connect to wss://api.meta.ai/v1/asr/realtime , send the handshake as the first JSON text frame within 10 seconds, then stream raw PCM as binary frames. This endpoint does not read the HTTP Authorization header; the credential travels in the handshake. Send {"type": "endStream"} to end input and keep reading until the server closes with 1000 .

Audio is sent as binary frames. The only client text frame after the handshake is the end-of-input marker, which half-closes the client-to-server direction and leaves the socket open so the server can flush pending results. Closing the socket instead also ends input, but can discard pending events.
